title: Check yourself: one builder, many networks

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A grocery chain's terminals all send field 22 as 051. At one lane a card's chip can't be read, so the cashier swipes it, and the integration fills the card fields from what the terminal actually read. What does the request carry?

options.text: Entry mode 051 with track 2 and no field 55, since field 22 and the card fields come from different places
options.says: the entry mode is fixed while the card fields follow the swipe, so the request claims a chip read and carries no chip data

options.text: Entry mode 051 with track 2 and field 55, since the failed chip read still produced its chip data
options.says: the stem says the card fields follow what the terminal read, a swipe, and a swipe produces track 2 and no chip data

options.text: Entry mode 901 with track 2 and no field 55, since jPOS corrects field 22 to match the fields present
options.says: jPOS doesn't rewrite fields to agree with each other; only one value that drives both field 22 and the card fields keeps them in step

options.text: Entry mode 901 with track 2 and no field 55, since the packager refuses 051 without field 55
options.says: a packager checks lengths when it packs, not whether fields agree with each other; the contradictory request packs and leaves

origin.section: 5.3 How the Card Was Read Decides the Card Fields

questions.stem: Your team will connect directly to a card scheme next quarter, and the licensed documents arrive in three weeks. To start testing now, a developer fills field 48 from a subelement layout found in a public forum post. What is the risk once that code goes live?

options.text: Little, since ISO 8583 defines the subelements of field 48 for the networks
options.says: ISO 8583 gives the private-use fields a number and a maximum length only; each network defines what goes inside

options.text: Little, since a host passes over subelements it doesn't recognise
options.says: a host reads the field by its own layout; a guessed layout is rejected or misread, not skipped

options.text: A rejection or a misread field, since only the network that owns the field decides its content
options.says: the layout lives in the licensed specification and nowhere else; a guess fails certification or is misread and surfaces later

options.text: A rejection or a warning in the host's log, since the host compares the field with the ISO standard
options.says: a rejection is possible, but ISO 8583 has no layout to compare the field with, and a guessed field the host can parse is accepted and misread

origin.section: 5.4 Private Fields Come From the Network's Specification, Behind One Hook

questions.stem: A gateway has visa-mux and mc-mux, each on its own link to its network's host. At 13:05 isConnected() is false on mc-mux and true on visa-mux, and a Mastercard purchase for 42.00 arrives from terminal 29110031. What should the gateway do with it?

options.text: Send it through visa-mux, since QMUX reads the card number and forwards the request to its network
options.says: QMUX writes every request to its one out queue; it doesn't look at the card and doesn't route

options.text: Send it through visa-mux, since the Visa host passes other networks' cards on to them
options.says: a network's host has no business with another network's card and acquirer ID; a decline is the good outcome

options.text: Report the Mastercard host unavailable at once, since nothing went out and nothing needs undoing
options.says: the purchase is checked against its own network's link before anything is sent, so the caller can be told at once

options.text: Report the Mastercard host unavailable and queue a reversal, since the purchase's outcome is unknown
options.says: nothing was sent, so the outcome is known: no purchase happened, and there is nothing to reverse

origin.section: 5.5 Each Network Is a Destination of Its Own

questions.stem: A direct link's specification says each message is preceded by a 2-byte binary length and nothing else. The client was deployed with VAPChannel and Base1Packager because "it's the Visa link". What does the host make of the client's first echo?

options.text: It unpacks the echo normally, since both frames start with the same 2-byte length
options.says: the length matches, but VAPChannel follows it with two zero bytes and a 22-byte header that this host doesn't expect

options.text: It unpacks the echo normally, since a host skips a header it didn't ask for
options.says: the host doesn't know a header is there; it reads every byte after the length as the message

options.text: It fails to unpack the echo, since the zero bytes and the header reach it as message bytes
options.says: the frame doesn't match the specification, so the host unpacks VAPChannel's padding and header as if they were the message

options.text: It fails to unpack the echo, since VAPChannel writes the length as four ASCII digits
options.says: VAPChannel writes a 2-byte binary length, as the captured frame shows; the trouble is what follows it

origin.section: 5.5.1 The Link Speaks the Network's Framing

concepts: A direct network link needs the channel whose frame matches the specification; VAPChannel adds two zero bytes and a 22-byte BASE I header after the length.
A QMUX does not route; each network's requests go through that network's MUX only, and a down link means host unavailable, never another network's link.
Private-use fields are defined only by each network's licensed specification and are kept behind one hook per network, never filled from a guess.
